prize_parts.citation: for the invention and development of the optical lattice clock, which brought time and frequency measurement to the 10^-18 level
for conceiving the cubic-kilometre IceCube detector and the discovery of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos, founding neutrino astronomy

statement.case_for: The two-part configuration pairs a precision-measurement advance with an observational discovery, both mature and independently confirmed. The optical lattice clock is a clean two-person attribution (Katori's magic-wavelength concept and first strontium demonstration; Ye's record accuracy and many-body clock work), has been replicated across Sr, Yb and Hg in several laboratories, and has consequences for tests of fundamental constants, relativistic geodesy and the redefinition of the second. IceCube's detection of a diffuse astrophysical neutrino flux, confirmed by independent analysis channels and followed by TXS 0506+056, NGC 1068 and the Galactic plane, opened a new observational window and is secure as a discovery even though individual source identifications remain at moderate significance. Neither achievement is adjacent to the 2025 superconducting-circuit award, and neither is likely to be judged early. Because the union is capped at three people, I reduce the IceCube credit to the intellectual leader of the programme rather than force an arbitrary trio.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is attribution for IceCube. The discovery is the product of a collaboration of hundreds and builds on AMANDA, Baikal and ANTARES, so naming only Halzen leaves out Karle and Yoshida, whom I credited in my opening ballot, and arguably other experimentalists, and a one-person credit invites the objection that the decisive work was collective and instrumental rather than individual. On the clock side, a technical rather than conceptual breakthrough that follows the 2005 frequency-comb prize and the 2012 ion-control prize could be judged incremental. Pairing two unrelated fields also dilutes each, and if the committee prefers a single coherent achievement, B043 alone or the moire-materials candidate B029 is cleaner.

responses.point: Kroll ranks optical lattice clocks first as an instrument-level advance in what can be measured and how accurately, notes that Katori's magic-wavelength concept is the decisive origin, and judges a separate prize defensible after the 2005 comb recognition.
responses.response: I agree, and it moved me from fourth place to the anchor of my configuration. As an instrumentalist I find the argument persuasive: the 10^-18 regime is reproduced by independent groups and compared internationally, which is the kind of confirmation I look for. Where I qualify Kroll is that the case rests on measurement impact rather than a new phenomenon, and the redefinition of the second has not happened, so I would pair the clock with a discovery-type achievement rather than treat it as the only sufficient prize.

responses.point: Olsson ranks magic-angle graphene first as a clear before-and-after discovery, but ranks IceCube seventh because a collaboration of hundreds makes a prize for up to three people hard to defend, though Halzen is the evident leader.
responses.response: The attribution objection to IceCube is fair and is the main reason I reduce my own opening trio to Halzen alone. I disagree that it should be disqualifying: the flux detection is secure, and Halzen's role as originator of the concept and scientific case is the least contested in the field. I take her point on graphene seriously, but I place it as an alternative because the origin of the superconductivity is unresolved, the work is eight years old, and Cao, Dean and others have claims that three names cannot cover.

responses.point: Johansson ranks circuit QED first as the architecture underlying superconducting quantum processors, following naturally from last year's circuits recognition, and suggests Wallraff, Schoelkopf and Girvin.
responses.response: The technological and scientific importance is not in doubt, but I read the same fact as Lindroth and Kroll do: the 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits makes a second superconducting-circuit award so soon a timing problem, and the four-name credit forces a difficult omission of Blais or Girvin. I rank it below my preferred parts and leave it out of the configuration.

responses.point: Danielsson ranks gamma-ray burst afterglows first as a clean, discovery-centred result that is mature and arguably overdue, while ranking IceCube second and noting entangled credit.
responses.response: I share the view that B033 is mature and overdue, and I ranked it third. I did not place it in the configuration because the credit is unresolved: van Paradijs is deceased and Piro, Djorgovski, Metzger and Frail all have claims, and the union cap of three people leaves no room to correct that. I would favour B033 over a weaker candidate if IceCube is rejected, but I have not seen a way to resolve its attribution better than IceCube's.

responses.point: Mehlig ranks fluctuation theorems first as a conceptual advance in statistical physics and ranks topological insulators second, with a theory pair plus the HgTe experiment.
responses.response: I agree on topological insulators, which I ranked second and keep as an alternative: confirmation is exceptionally broad and recognition is arguably overdue. My qualification is the one Eriksson and Lindroth raise, that Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang, Fu and Moore are not covered and the 2016 prize on topological phases raises a marginal-novelty question. I do not rank fluctuation theorems as high as Mehlig does; only he supports the candidate, and I cannot judge the priority questions among Evans, Jarzynski, Crooks and Seifert.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will accept a one-person credit for IceCube, or whether a trio such as Halzen, Karle and Yoshida would require dropping the clock part.
Whether Katori and Ye plus a single IceCube laureate is the best use of the three-person cap compared with a single three-person achievement such as B029 or B008.
Priority and credit within IceCube, AMANDA and the earlier deep-water neutrino pioneers cannot be settled from the supplied material.
Whether B043 and B010 are sufficiently distinct in standing to share a prize without one appearing subordinate.
statement.conflict_note: My profile documents work on PAMELA, Fermi-LAT, PoGOLite/PoGO+ and XL-Calibur, so astroparticle and gamma-ray instrumentation, including the neutrino and gamma-ray burst candidates B010 and B033, is close to my own field and the committee should note this. No personal or institutional tie to any named candidate is apparent from the provided profile, and I do not see a specific recusal requirement.
